answer: Each bonded identity escrows collateral; when proofs show k identities coordinated in equivocation, pairwise correlation triggers penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, hence O(k²), rather than treating each signer independently. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss through asymmetric depreciation, making Sybil expansion costly. A vine of linked keys cannot evade evidence: conflicting signatures on a relic record or a sonnet are attributable to the same accountable set.
